We decompose the fraction into a sum of partial fractions, as follows:

$$
\frac{6-5s}{{s}^{2}+9}=\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+9}-\frac{5s}{{s}^{2}+9}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡3t} & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0, \\ L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+9}-\frac{5s}{{s}^{2}+9}} & =2{L}^{-1}{\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9}}-5{L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}} \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t-5\operatorname{cos}⁡3t.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{6-5s}{{s}^{2}+9}$ is $f(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t-5\operatorname{cos}⁡3t.$
